dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: I have a question for everyone. Where were you and what were you doing when WKU announced the exam postponement last November?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I was sitting at my desk trying to finish my essay. I was typing the conclusion when I got the notification. I literally jumped up.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I was sleeping. I found out in the morning when Rustam sent me a voice message at seven a.m. I couldn't believe it.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: I was practising football in the corridor — yes, in the corridor — when Amir's message arrived. I dropped the ball completely.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Ha! I was having a shower. My phone was buzzing on the shelf. When I finally checked it, I had fourteen messages.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Fourteen? That's nothing. I was getting sixty messages per minute in the group chat.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: What was everyone saying in the chat?

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Half the group was celebrating. The other half was panicking because they had already studied everything and didn't want to wait.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: That's so true. I was feeling relieved and guilty at the same time. I hadn't prepared enough for that exam.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I was feeling pure joy. I wasn't ready at all. I was planning to stay up all night.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: The best reaction was Rustam sending three laughing emojis while someone was crying in the chat.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: I maintain that it was the correct response. Sometimes laughing is the only thing you can do.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Anyway — do you remember that night in the hallway? That's a memory I will never forget. Everyone sitting on the floor with tea.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I was telling stories about blackouts back home. And Rustam was scaring everyone with ghost stories.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: I was not scaring anyone. I was simply... sharing cultural narratives.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: You made Zhibek hide behind a pillow. That counts as scaring.

questions.text: "I ___ the conclusion when I got the notification." Choose the correct form.
questions.hint: Longer background action = Past Continuous: "was typing". Shorter interrupting event = PS: "got the notification".

questions.text: "What ___ you ___ when the power went out?" Complete the question.
questions.hint: "What were you doing when...?" — Past Continuous question: were + subject + verb-ing.

questions.text: "She ___ a shower when the phone buzzed." Choose the correct form.
questions.hint: Background action in progress = Past Continuous: "was having a shower." Phone buzzing = shorter Past Simple event.

questions.text: "Half the group was celebrating when the other half was panicking." This describes two simultaneous past actions.
questions.hint: Two Past Continuous actions happening at the same time = both use "was/were + -ing". Often connected with "while".

questions.text: "He dropped the ball when the message ___." Choose the correct form.
questions.hint: The message arriving = short, sudden event = Past Simple. He was practising = background = Past Continuous.
"While" + Past Continuous + Past Continuous = two simultaneous background actions.

questions.text: Which question correctly asks about a past action in progress?
questions.hint: "What were you doing?" = Past Continuous question. Asks about an ongoing action at a past moment.

questions.text: "I was planning to stay up all night." This Past Continuous describes:
opts: An intended action that may not have happened
questions.correct: An intended action that may not have happened
questions.hint: "was planning to" = future intention in the past — at that time, that was the plan. The postponement changed it!
